[F3 F6 F7] [NS-1]

[F7 F3 F11] [NS-1 NS-0]

Asks: refund_full $5.00

what_would_change: Had the driver confirmed arrival more than 200 m away, left before 5 minutes, or not both messaged and called the rider, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled the trip for a reason of his own — a flat tyre — and told the rider so himself: "Sorry, tyre puncture, car got problem, have to cancel" (F11), repeated in his written statement "then my tyre went flat, so I had to cancel" (F14). No cancellation reason was picked in the app (F4), so his own words are the only reason on record.
Because the cancellation was for the driver's own reason and not for a rider no-show, NS-1 does not apply and the $5.00 cancellation fee charged to the rider (F8) must be refunded in full.

Even if NS-1 were applied, condition (iii) would still be read against the fee only on the driver's side of the record; the point for the rider is that the driver was stationary at 40 m from the pickup from 22:35:45 until he cancelled at 22:41:35 (F3, F6, F7), so nothing in the timeline shows the rider refusing to come out before he gave up on his own car.

The driver's own words exclude a no-show reading: he had already tapped "I'm Here" 40 m from the pickup (F7) and remained there 5 min 50 s (F3), and his stated cause of cancellation is the vehicle, not the rider — the rider's complaint that "by the time I came out he had cancelled" is consistent with his 22:41 cancellation message (F11).

The driver's no-show history (1 upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days, F19) does not decide this case but supports the charge being reviewed on his record; the rider profile is clean with 0 disputes in 90 days (F18).

weaknesses: The GPS record does show the driver within 200 m of the pickup from 22:35:30 and stationary 40 m away for 5 min 50 s (F2, F3, F7), which the other side will use to argue NS-1(i) and (iv) are satisfied and that the wait was genuinely served.

The driver sent 2 in-app messages and made 1 in-app call before cancelling (F5, F13), so the other side will argue NS-1(iii) is met; the call log shows the rider did not answer (F13), which they will read as the rider not being available.

The 5-minute free wait had elapsed (5 min 50 s after arrival, F6), so the other side will say the threshold was crossed and the $5.00 fee was properly chargeable apart from the driver's own reason for cancelling.
No cancellation reason was picked in the app (F4), so there is no app-side record of a no-show cancellation to contradict the driver's claim that he was waiting for the rider.

claims.assertion: The driver was physically at the pickup point: GPS puts his closest approach at 38 m (F1), he was first within 200 m at 22:35:30 and stayed within 200 m for a cumulative 6 min 5 s (F2), stationary at 40 m from the pickup from 22:35:45 until the 22:41:35 cancellation (F3), satisfying NS-1(i).

The free-wait requirement was met: the platform recorded arrival ("I'm Here") at 22:35:45 and the driver cancelled only 5 min 50 s later at 22:41:35 (F6, F7), which exceeds the 5-minute free wait counted from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival (F4), satisfying NS-1(ii).

The contact requirement was met: before cancelling the driver sent 2 in-app messages (first 22:36:15) and made 1 in-app call (first 22:37:15) (F5), including the message "I'm here at the pickup point, blue Toyota Prius." (F10) and the unanswered call at 22:37 (F13), satisfying NS-1(iii).

The driver remained at the pickup point throughout the wait and until cancellation (F3, F7), so there is no GPS gap leaving presence unproven under NS-1(iv); the only reason he left was the tyre failure.

The driver did not cancel for a reason of his own that voids the fee: his message at 22:41 "Sorry, tyre puncture, car got problem, have to cancel." (F11) and his statement (F14) describe an unforeseen vehicle defect occurring after arrival and after the wait, not a refusal of the trip, another job, or a personal matter; the app records no reason picked (F4), and the car waiting and the rider's non-appearance are not NS-3 reasons.

No mitigating or safety element changes the analysis: no traffic incidents were recorded and conditions were fair (F16, F17), the trip carried no surge (F9), and the rider's complaint contains no allegation of dangerous driving, harassment or threat requiring SAFE-1 escalation.
The $5.00 fee on record (F8, F4) is the official cancellation fee payable to the driver when a rider no-show cancellation is upheld (NS-1 / §2.2), so the charge should stand as `no_action`.

weaknesses: NS-1(i) requires GPS within 200 m of the pickup: the driver never reached the pickup point itself, his closest approach was 38 m (F1) and he waited 40 m away (F3) — the rider may argue he was not at the pickup and that the threshold should be read strictly.

The driver never picked a cancellation reason in the app (F4), and the tyre-puncture reason appears only after the fact (F11, F14); the rider may argue the real cause was that he gave up and drove off rather than the rider failing to show.

The rider's complaint says 'by the time I came out he had cancelled' (no supporting GPS/timeline fact on the rider's own timing is in the record), so the rider may argue the 5 min 50 s wait was shorter than the record's arrival-to-cancellation gap suggests.

The driver carries 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days (F19); while RD-6/NS-9 flag rules attach to repeat route deviations and rider no-shows (F19 also shows 1259 trips in 90 d), the rider may use the history to attack credibility.

points.response: Conceded on the facts: GPS does place the driver within 200 m from 22:35:30 and stationary 40 m from the pickup (F2, F3), so NS-1(i) is not the rider's point — the rider's case turns on why he cancelled, not on where he parked.
Conceded: arrival was recorded at 22:35:45 and cancellation came 5 min 50 s later (F6, F7), so the wait threshold in NS-1(ii) was crossed; the rider does not dispute the clock.

Conceded: 2 in-app messages (first 22:36:15) and 1 in-app call (first 22:37:15) were made before cancelling (F5), so NS-1(iii) is met on its terms; the call went unanswered (F13) but the requirement is an attempt, not an answer.
Conceded on continuity: the stationary GPS block runs 22:35:45–22:41:35 with no gap (F3, F7), so NS-1(iv) raises no missing-record point against the rider.

This is the whole case and the driver's own words defeat him: "Sorry, tyre puncture, car got problem, have to cancel" (F11) and his statement "then my tyre went flat, so I had to cancel" (F14) give a reason of his own — the vehicle — for cancelling, which is exactly what NS-0/NS-3 treat as not a rider no-show; the app picked no reason (F4), so no record attributes the cancellation to the rider.

Agreed there is no traffic or safety element (F16, F17, F9); that is neutral, not helpful to the driver — with no traffic excuse and no rider-side cause, the only cause on the record is his own car (F11, F14), which voids the fee under NS-3.

The $5.00 fee (F4, F8) is payable only for a driver cancellation for rider no-show (NS-1), and the driver's own reason was the tyre failure (F11, F14), so NS-3 applies and the fee must be refunded in full under NS-2/NS-3, not upheld.

On the driver's own weakness about the late reason: the tyre explanation appears only at 22:41, after the 5 min 50 s wait had run (F11, F6), which shows he had already decided to end the trip for his own reason and the no-show label is being fitted to it after the event.

His words describe a car defect discovered after the wait had already been served, not a reason of his own for refusing the trip: he was at the pickup from 22:35:45, messaged the rider at 22:36 (F10), called at 22:37 (F13), and cancelled only at 22:41:35 when the tyre failed (F11, F14) — NS-1's own conditions already settle the waiting, the car and the pickup location, and the reading question excludes those from being 'a reason of his own'.

NS-1 does apply: all four conditions hold — presence within 200 m and 38 m closest approach (F1, F2), wait of 5 min 50 s from recorded arrival (F6, F7), 2 in-app messages and 1 in-app call before cancelling (F5), and continuous presence at the pickup (F3) — so the $5.00 fee charged on record (F8) stands under NS-1 / §2.2.

Nothing here helps the rider: the same record (F3, F6, F7) shows the driver served the full free wait at 40 m and cancelled only after it elapsed, which is exactly what NS-1(ii) requires for the fee to stand.

His stated cause of cancellation being the vehicle does not extinguish a no-show cancellation under NS-0: he had arrived, waived the wait and attempted contact (F7, F3, F11), and no record shows the rider came out or responded before 22:41:35 (F5, F13).
